Friendzy / Classic party games / Two Truths and a Lie

How to play Two Truths and a Lie

Two real. One fake. Can you tell? The classic. Each player shares three statements about themselves — two completely true, one convincing lie. The group debates and votes on which one is the lie. You'll learn unexpected things.

2–10 players~12 minRevealing & FunSocial & discussion games🚗 Works in the car

How to play

  1. Each player thinks of two true facts about themselves and one believable lie.
  2. They share all three statements in any order.
  3. The group discusses and debates — then everyone votes simultaneously on the lie.
  4. Reveal the truth. Anyone who guessed correctly gets a point.
  5. Rotate until everyone has gone.

Example round

  • 'I've met a president' / 'I've never broken a bone' / 'I was in a commercial as a kid'
  • The lie: 'I've never broken a bone' — but the commercial seemed most suspicious.
  • Best lies: things that sound slightly unbelievable but are plausible for that person.

Tips

  • Make your lie the most boring-sounding one — it's harder to question.
  • React the same way to all three when asked follow-up questions.
